Anyone who loves this will not be allowed around my children I'm exaggerating of course but fo real I did not laugh once. While the "offensiveness" isn't the basis of my distaste, I have thoughts on it. I get that they're probably mocking the racism Walter espouses but I must have missed the irony cuz most of his comments just kind of hung there without a punchline. Also the "stfu donny" bit got old after the first time. Everything I found sexist seemed void of any attempt at humor--the pointless nudity seemed like typical horny man movie vibes. Regardless of intentions, it's typically not good satire when the people most likely to watch your movie (conservative white men) can laugh without catching the irony. At the end of the day, the only non-white character is literally a white actor with a cartoonish accent, so the commentary is diluted. I liked Brandt, he was funny. The Dude was solid but mostly just existed and had a couple fun quotes. More than anything this just wasn't my type of humor; truly no hate to those that do get the irony and enjoy it.

I really didn’t find it funny as so many people claimed. In the end the case of the money doesn’t get resolved as cripple Lebowski keeps it for himself. Another complain I had was we never went deeper into “the dude’s” backstory. Donny’s character dynamic got old very quickly, Walter was just overall annoying, and Donny’s death felt very forced. Overall I thought this movie was something more than what it actually was and I don’t understand the hype behind it. The cowboy was cool tho

QUOTES • Those are good burgers Shut the fuck up Donny • I still jerk off manually • I’m The Dude • Yeah, well you know, that’s just like, your opinion man • That rug really tied the room together • I can’t be worrying about that shit, life goes on man NOTES One of my good friends Ryan Garner and I are doing a monthly movie review. This month’s theme was comedy and this was his pick. I’ve known Ryan since I was 15. He was a pallbearer for Whitney. He was one of the first people I called about my parents. He’s always been there for me. A really good friend. It was his house that I went to when my mom kicked me out at 15 (for doing what every 15 year old does). REVIEW Seeing Walter pull the gun at the bowling alley was rough. All I think about is my parents pulling their guns when I see guns. And the ashes at the end was rough too. Whitney is buried in West Jordan across from Gardner village. My dad is in a keychain I keep in my gym, along with the rest of his ashes in the urn from the mortuary. It’s incredibly hard to put the souls you loved most in a casket or an urn. I’ll never forget seeing my dad’s death certificate “shot in head”. Death really fucks with one’s mind. Sometimes I want to do something cool with my dad’s ashes and other times I’m so fucking pissed at him that I just don’t care about it. One day I think I’ll spread what’s in the keychain over Whitney’s resting spot so they can be together. After my dad would get done with his 2nd shift he would go to her graveside at night. My dad loved Whitney more than any parent loves their kid. And he loved me too. He had the biggest heart. My mom is still at my grandparents and idgaf what happens to her ashes. I hated seeing Jeff Bridges play the dude when to me he’s Kevin Flynn from Tron, who I compare to my Dad. And also Professor Lupin play a weirdo when to me he’ll always be Lupin who I also compare to my dad. The mom from crazy stupid love plays a weirdo too. Just an odd movie. Not my sense of humor. Too much hem and haw, the dialogue is so awkward and not thought out. And although I like some stupid movies. At least it’s regular guys in funny situations. Not dumb asses in a bad situation. Nobody knows anybody like the guys in this movie which makes it feel unrelateable.

There were a lot of great elements to this, but it didn’t amount to anything. Like the humor is almost there but just misses being my thing. The plot was a bit too confusing for its own good, very much things are just happening. I’m sure it’s an intentional chaos but I wish I liked it more.
